_comment: v0.15 T4.4: THE regional-work canonical. The adversarial playtest found zero repeatable work outside Liscor -- every pilgrimage region was a place you visited once. Each now carries one job prop on the serving_tray idiom (once_per_waking + gold, banked under interactions.gd's `serve:` key): riverfarm_field_board (3,10), parlor_errand_slate (5,1), forge_fetch_slips (18,4). This run proves all three PAY, all three REFUSE a second take in the same waking, the exact gold ledger across them (60 -> 62 -> 64 -> 66, then 68 on the re-armed board), and that a sleep RE-ARMS the first of them -- which is the whole claim the word 'repeatable' makes. Teleport-based between regions on the pallass_peek precedent: the routes into all three are proven live by their own region walkthroughs, and the subject here is the job machinery, not the travel. near_pallass fixture: 60 gold, no brothers_marker (so the slate's marker-rate variant is provably unmatched -- the can-fail side), no perfect_hospitality (so no +1 wage rider on the once_per_waking arm).

steps._comment: == RIVERFARM: the field-work board (3,10), at the fence line south of the paddock. North approach (3,11), bump south. ==

payload_contains.text: You take a scrap off its hook and spend the morning behind it. Ditching, mostly. The village pays coin because coin is the thing it has least of, and it pays on the day.

steps._comment: == THE REFUSAL: a second take in the SAME waking pays nothing and banks nothing. entity_first_use is keyed `serve:riverfarm_field_board`, and interactions.gd banks that key BEFORE resolving effects, so the refusal can never burn the wage. ==
steps.name: interact

payload_contains.text: Every hook is bare. Riverfarm doesn't invent work to keep a stranger busy.

steps._comment: == INVRISIL: the Brothers' errand slate (5,1), between the cots and the counter. South approach (5,2), bump north. brothers_marker is unbanked at this fixture, so the BASE 2-gold line reads and the marker-rate variant is proven unmatched. ==

payload_contains.text: You take the top line off the slate and walk it across Invrisil, no questions asked at either end. Two gold in your hand, and behind you a wet cloth is already going over the line.
The slate is wiped clean. Come back when the chalk's been busy.

steps._comment: == PALLASS: the forge tier's fetch slips (18,4), east of the second bench. South approach (18,5) -- the seam's blocked run stops at x=17, so this cell is open. ==

payload_contains.text: You take a slip, walk its stock number down to the racks and the finished piece back up. The clerk who pays you writes down the hour you took, to the quarter.
The rack is empty until the next shift files its slips.

steps._comment: == THE SLEEP: the delivery_loop/board_loop bed precedent (teleport to your_bed, the walk is proven elsewhere). This is what makes the three props REPEATABLE rather than three one-shot coins. ==
== RE-ARMED: the same board, a new waking, a second real bank and a second real wage. ==

assert_event_count, not assert_event_logged: the outbound leg already logged a bump on this cell, so a bare `logged` here would pass on the FIRST one and prove nothing about this walk. Two bumps = both legs really faced the board.
The ledger's last rung: the second field-work wage really was PAID, not just banked. 60 -> 62 -> 64 -> 66 -> 68 across four jobs and one sleep.
Scope guard: regional odd jobs are work, not adventure -- nothing in this run picks a fight.
